content: Cómo REDUCIR LOS 50 MIL CASOS ANUALES DE CÁNCER DE MAMAS QUE SE PRESENTAN EN EL PERÚ? Dr. Gilmar Grisson  ginecólogo oncologo de la Liga contra el cáncer... The best way to reduce cancer figures in our country is through health promotion and preventive check-ups. This implies greater consumption of fresh vegetables, more fish and poultry, less red meat; as well as avoiding saturated fats and processed foods which contribute to various types of cancers. All women should perform monthly self-examinations starting at age 24 years old. If any nodules or masses are found, its crucial to consult a doctor immediately for further evaluation. Women need annual mammograms—the most effective screening tool—for early detection. Thus, even small tumors could potentially allow breast conservation surgery. Sometimes chemotherapy isnt necessary either. Eight out of ten cases of breast cancer occur spontaneously here in Peru, meaning there’s no family history involved. Only about three percent have genetic predispositions while fifteen percent might have familial links. Therefore, many Peruvians remain vulnerable despite lacking symptoms or known risk factors within their families. Prevention remains key since numerous individuals neglect regular screenings until experiencing discomfort prompting specialist visits. Promoting healthy diets alongside prevention strategies would help mitigate diverse forms of cancer across populations. It falls upon state responsibility to enhance information dissemination along with free preventative campaigns against breast cancer specifically.

headline: Elecciones en Argentina
